subject: Nova Health — regions, subprocessors, and evidence request
messages:
From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@novahealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@novahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-18 09:12 -0700
Subject: Questions on processing locations and subprocessor evidence

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Nova Health is interested in Redwood for clinical summarization in our patient portal, but our InfoSec and Legal teams have a few immediate questions before we move to procurement: 

1) For API requests that include PHI (patient identifiers + notes), where is the data processed and persisted? We need a clear mapping of which regions handle inference, caching, and logs.
2) Which subprocessors handle any intermediate processing, storage, or monitoring? We need their legal company names, locations, and SOC2 status if available.
3) Are there any cross-border transfers (e.g., US<->EU) for requests originating in the US or vice versa? We need to understand if any routing may send derivative data outside the region.
4) What is Redwood's standard retention for request logs, embeddings, and KV caches? Can we request deletion on demand and is there an audit trail?

Ideally we need a short packet (inventory + diagram + acceptable contract language) to present to our procurement and legal teams by EOD Tuesday. Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Lucia
Lucia Gomez
Director, Information Security
Nova Health

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@novahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on processing locations and subprocessor evidence

Hi Lucia — great questions and thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: we can provide a region-by-region processing map, a current subprocessor inventory with SOC2/ISO statuses, and a retention/deletion playbook including on-demand deletion and audit logs. See details below and attached packet.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_inventory_20270418.pdf (inventory + SOC2 notes), redwood_data_path_diagram_20270418.png (logical data flows), sla_addendum_draft_0.1.docx (example contract language for retention/deletion)

High-level responses:
- Processing locations: For hosted deployments, inference is executed in the region indicated by the customer's routing policy. For customers on our Hosted API with default routing, requests from the US are served from our us-west-2 and us-east-1 clusters only; no EU inference nodes are involved unless routing is explicitly configured. Persistent logs and long-term artifacts (embeddings, retained request logs) are stored in the region selected for the account; for Nova Health we recommend pinning to us-east-1 to keep all artifacts in the US.
- Subprocessors: The attached inventory lists subprocessors and their operating jurisdictions. Key categories: cloud IaaS (US/EU), monitoring & observability (US), encryption key management (KMS — US only by default), and third-party model optimization partners (contracted vendors; some operate in EU).
- Cross-border transfers: By default, we do not export US-hosted customer artifacts to the EU. We do, however, run certain model optimization jobs and managed batch inference workflows on partner infra that may operate in EMEA if customers choose multi-region routing or dedicated capacity in those regions. See diagram for conditional paths.
- Retention & deletion: Default retention for request logs is 90 days; embeddings are retained 365 days unless opt-out is configured. We support immediate on-demand deletion requests via API and a signed support ticket; deletions are logged and an audit record is emitted to account admins. The SLA addendum doc contains the sample contract language we usually provide.

Next steps: Marissa/Neha — can you validate the SOC2/ISO flags in the inventory and confirm the expected time to produce signed evidence (e.g., SOC2 attestation, subprocessor contracts)? Stephanie — can you review the SLA language and flag anything Nova Health will likely want tightened (retention periods, deletion verification artifacts)?

Lucia — at minimum we can get the packet and the diagram to you by EOD tomorrow (Tuesday) and set up a short call to walk through the conditional transfer paths. If that works, I can send a calendar invite with a proposed 30-minute slot.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@novahealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@novahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-18 14:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on processing locations and subprocessor evidence

Thanks — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from Legal: 

- For health data, Nova's baseline requires that PHI not leave the US. Can Redwood guarantee that if we select a US-only routing policy and pin to us-east-1, no processing or derived artifacts will be sent to EU subprocessors (including ModelTune GmbH) without our prior written consent?
- For on-demand deletions, Legal wants an SLA clause that includes a deletion confirmation with timestamped audit trail and optionally a third-party verification step for an extra fee. Can you confirm whether the delete API returns an audit token we can store and whether Redwood will emit a verifiable event to our SIEM?

We'd like the packet and the SOC2 redacted summary by EOD tomorrow. Also please include an explicit statement we can include in the MSA: "Customer data and derived artifacts will not be transferred to subprocessors outside the US except with Customer's prior written consent."

—Lucia

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@novahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-19 15:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on processing locations and subprocessor evidence

Hi Lucia — quick confirmations and next steps: 

- US-only guarantee: Yes — if Nova Health requests a US-only routing policy and picks a US region (we recommend us-east-1), we will enforce policy to ensure inference and artifact persistence remain in the US. ModelTune GmbH and other EU partners will not receive raw requests or embeddings unless Nova explicitly signs up for multi-region/dedicated capacity that includes EMEA. We'll include the explicit MSA clause you proposed in the SLA addendum and mark it as negotiable with Legal Ops.
- Deletion API / audit token: Our deletion endpoint returns a unique deletion-id and a signed timestamped event which we can push to the customer's configured SIEM (via syslog/HTTPS) and store in our audit ledger. We'll add language to the addendum describing the deletion confirmation format and the optional third-party verification workflow (costed).

Deliverables we will send by EOD tomorrow: 
1) Redacted SOC2 Type II summary (PDF) — prepared by Marissa.
2) Subprocessor inventory (attached updated PDF).
3) Data path diagram with conditional routing callouts (attached PNG).
4) SLA addendum draft with the US-only clause and deletion audit wording for Legal review.

I'll send a 30-minute walkthrough invite for Wednesday 10:00am ET — please let me know if that slot works for you.

Thanks,
Karthik
